title: Visuospatial Rotation
shortDescription: Mental rotation of 3D objects — identify which option is the same shape rotated, not a mirrored fake.
longDescription: Visuospatial Rotation is built on the Mental Rotation Test paradigm (Vandenberg & Kuse, 1978; originating from Shepard & Metzler, 1971) — the classic measure of the ability to mentally rotate a shape and recognize it from a different orientation. You're shown a target shape and must pick which option is a genuine rotation of it, rejecting mirrored (chirality-flipped) look-alikes — the core challenge the paradigm is built around.
sourceNote: Every target and option is a real, programmatically generated and rendered SVG (asymmetric 2D polygons, embedded as data URIs — no external asset pipeline needed), verified visually by rendering to PNG during authoring. Two adaptations from the original Vandenberg & Kuse test, both noted transparently: (1) it uses original 2D asymmetric polygons rather than the original's 3D cube-block figures, since 2D shapes with a genuine chirality (mirroring produces a different-handed shape than any rotation) test the same core rotation-vs-mirror discrimination without needing 3D rendering/projection — a simplification used by several digital cognitive-test platforms; (2) each item is single-correct-answer multiple choice rather than the original's "select the 2 of 4 matches," a common adaptation for deterministic auto-scoring. Distractors are generated three ways per item — wrong rotation amount, mirrored at the correct angle, and mirrored at a wrong angle — so guessing based on rotation alone or mirroring alone isn't enough.

sections.name: Rotation Trials
sections.description: Identify the option that is a true rotation of the target shape, not a mirrored version.
sections.instructions: Mentally rotate the target shape and compare it to each option. Exactly one option is the same shape, just rotated — the others are either rotated by the wrong amount or mirrored.

scoringDimensions.label: Mental Rotation
scoringDimensions.description: Ability to mentally rotate a shape and distinguish a true rotation from a mirrored look-alike.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Distinguishing a true rotation from a mirrored look-alike is difficult right now — a very common starting point, since mirror-image confusion is exactly what this paradigm is designed to probe.
recommendations: Trace one distinctive feature (a notch or corner) on the target and track where it ends up after rotating in your head, rather than judging the whole shape's silhouette at once
Practice with physical objects (rotate a real asymmetric object like a shoe or a hand) to build the underlying spatial-transformation skill
Slow down specifically on options that look 'almost right' — those are usually the mirrored distractors

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Catches obvious mismatches but the closely-matched mirrored distractors still cause errors.
recommendations: Practice specifically on mirror-vs-rotation discrimination — cover the target and try to redraw it rotated before looking at the options
Pick one asymmetric feature as your anchor and check it first on every option before considering the rest

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: Reliably identifies true rotations and rejects mirrored distractors on most trials.
recommendations: Push your speed on easier trials — accuracy is already solid there
Notice whether larger rotation angles (further from the target's original orientation) slow you down more — that's a normal, well-documented pattern

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: Fast, accurate rotation-vs-mirror discrimination across nearly every trial, including the harder rotation angles.
recommendations: This is a strong, genuine spatial-reasoning advantage — fields like engineering, design, and surgery lean on exactly this skill
Compare this result with Spatial Intelligence's matrix-reasoning score — they draw on related but distinct spatial skills

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Near-perfect mental rotation performance across every trial and angle tested.
recommendations: This is an elite spatial-rotation result — notice where it shows up as a real advantage in 3D-reasoning-heavy work
Consider fields that specifically reward strong 3D spatial reasoning under time pressure
